analyst_view.overall: Early view: Liverpool under Andoni Iraola are fourth after winning 3-1 at Palace, but they have scored only four league goals in five games at Anfield and could not land a shot on target at home to Arsenal. Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 last time out and play in the Europa League on 26 November. Liverpool should control this, but their home finishing is the big question.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Liverpool's home attack has been weak, with four goals in five Anfield league games, and Hugo Ekitike is out with an Achilles injury. Sunderland have scored only eight all season, so a 1-0 or 2-0 home win looks more likely than a goal-fest.

corners.text: The site has 9.9 corners. I lean higher: Liverpool tend to camp in the opponent's half (17 efforts against Arsenal), and Sunderland under Regis Le Bris will defend deep at Anfield. Sustained pressure against a low block usually brings plenty of corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I agree: Sunderland will pick up some bookings while defending for long spells, and their physical, intense approach beat Chelsea, but Liverpool should have so much of the ball that they will have little reason to foul. Nothing points strongly either way.

shots.text: The site has 32.4 shots, which is very high. I lean lower: Liverpool will take a lot of shots, but 21.5 for them plus 10.9 for a Sunderland side with eight goals in 10 games is too many. High 20s fits better.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Liverpool forced no saves at home to Arsenal despite 17 efforts, and the analysis of Iraola's side says Isak gets little service. Plenty of shots, but many from distance or blocked.
